entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: %s does not accept a subquery argument
entries.rationale: unreachable: a PromQL function that takes a range-vector argument is either a member of the shared range-window vocabulary (chplan.IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc, consulted through canonicalRangeWindowFunc so the double_exponential_smoothing source spelling resolves to its IR name) or absent_over_time, and the arm directly above this guard routes absent_over_time to lowerAbsentOverTimeOverSubquery, so no parseable query reaches it

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over %T is unsupported
entries.rationale: SubqueryExpr.Expr must type-check as an instant vector, and every instant-vector AST shape is dispatched (selector, call, paren, aggregate, binary, unary, plus the parser-impossible nested SubqueryExpr handled defensively); scalar- and string-typed inners are parse-time type errors. The lowerHistogramNativeSubqueryInner call added ahead of the switch by cerberus issue #2543 does not narrow that exhaustiveness claim: when it returns matched=false control falls through to the identical switch this rationale already covers, over the identical e.Expr value.

guard: past returning if plan, matched, err := lowerHistogramNativeSubqueryInner(e, step, s, ctx); matched

past exhaustive switch inner := e.Expr.(type) over [case *parser.VectorSelector; case *parser.Call; case *parser.ParenExpr; case *parser.AggregateExpr; case *parser.BinaryExpr; case *parser.UnaryExpr; case *parser.SubqueryExpr]

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over aggregation of %T is unsupported
entries.rationale: An aggregation's argument must type-check as an instant vector, and every instant-vector AST shape is dispatched (paren, call, selector, binary, unary, nested aggregate); scalar- and string-typed inners are parse-time type errors.

guard: past exhaustive switch inner := expr.(type) over [case *parser.ParenExpr; case *parser.Call; case *parser.VectorSelector; case *parser.BinaryExpr; case *parser.UnaryExpr; case *parser.AggregateExpr]

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over absent() requires query eval-time context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: The HTTP handlers always thread eval times via LowerAt / LowerAtRange; only the raw Lower() entrypoint (tests / tooling) can present a zero eval anchor to this guard.

guard: default of switch agg.Op over [case parser.TOPK, parser.BOTTOMK, parser.LIMITK; case parser.COUNT_VALUES; case parser.LIMIT_RATIO; case parser.SUM, parser.COUNT, parser.AVG, parser.MIN, parser.MAX, parser.STDDEV, parser.STDVAR, parser.GROUP, parser.QUANTILE; default]

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery inner %s expects exactly %d argument(s), got %d
entries.rationale: the range-window vocabulary gate above (chplan.IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc) routes a non-reducer call to lowerSubqueryOverInstantCall, so only vocabulary members reach this check, and subqueryInnerRangeFnShape reports each member's true PromQL arity; none of them is variadic, so the upstream parser has already rejected any call whose argument count differs before lowering begins

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery inner %s must wrap a MatrixSelector, got %T
entries.rationale: matrixArgExpr is peelWrappers(call.Args[matrixArg]) (#1896); the parser only ever gives this argument position a Matrix-typed expression (a MatrixSelector or a SubqueryExpr, optionally wrapped in ParenExpr/StepInvariantExpr), and peeling strips every such wrapper, so after peeling matrixArgExpr can only be a MatrixSelector or a SubqueryExpr -- this assertion cannot fail on any parseable query

guard: past returning if innerSub, ok := matrixArgExpr.(*parser.SubqueryExpr); ok

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery inner matrix selector must wrap a VectorSelector, got %T
entries.rationale: the parser only ever builds a MatrixSelector around a VectorSelector, so the inner assertion cannot fail on any parseable query

guard: past returning if innerSub, ok := matrixArgExpr.(*parser.SubqueryExpr); ok

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery inner %s is evaluated per anchor and requires a query evaluation time (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: subqueryGridCtx reports no grid only when no evaluation anchor was threaded through, which the HTTP handlers never do: every wire query lowers through LowerAt, LowerAtRange or LowerAtRangeOpts, and only the bare Lower entry point used by package tests leaves the anchor unset

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over %s K: %w
entries.rationale: error-propagation wrapper (%w): the wrapped rejection is raised by lowerScalarArg and is catalogued at its origin. The registerScalarGuard arm above it returns its own error directly and never reaches this wrap, so now that the K domain is enforced at execution time nothing this wrapper carries is a domain rejection.

guard: else of if kF, ok := tryScalarLiteral(agg.Param); ok
past returning if err := registerScalarGuard(ctx, agg.Op.String()+" K", agg.Param, s, func(values []float64) error { _, err := aggregationParamDomain(values) return err }); err != nil

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery `@ start()` modifier requires query range context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: the query endpoints always lower through LowerAtRange with the request window, so range context is present. Cerberus issue #2581 added two new callers, lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubqueryFoldFn and lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubquerySelectFn (histogram_native_mixed_or_subquery_aggregate_range_fn.go) — both reached only from the same query-endpoint entry points as every other caller in this list, so the claim is unaffected.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery `@ end()` modifier requires query range context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: the query endpoints always lower through LowerAtRange with the request window, so range context is present. Cerberus issue #2581 added two new callers, lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubqueryFoldFn and lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubquerySelectFn (histogram_native_mixed_or_subquery_aggregate_range_fn.go) — both reached only from the same query-endpoint entry points as every other caller in this list, so the claim is unaffected.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: unexpected subquery StartOrEnd token %v
entries.rationale: the PromQL parser yields only START, END, or zero in StartOrEnd. Cerberus issue #2581 added two new callers, lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubqueryFoldFn and lowerSumOrAvgMixedOrSubquerySelectFn (histogram_native_mixed_or_subquery_aggregate_range_fn.go), both threading the same parser-produced SubqueryExpr through unchanged, so the claim is unaffected.

guard: default of switch e.StartOrEnd over [case parser.START; case parser.END; case 0; default]
